findings.title: Adding an abstract SPI method breaks existing CryptoProvider implementations
findings.body: CryptoProvider is a public ServiceLoader SPI, but `order()` was added as an abstract method. Any provider compiled against the previous interface can still be discovered at runtime, but `CryptoIntegration.detectProvider()` now invokes this missing method and will fail with AbstractMethodError, preventing startup. Make this a default method with a safe default priority (or otherwise provide a compatibility path) so existing external providers remain usable.

findings.title: Crypto provider selection is nondeterministic when providers have equal priority
findings.body: The selection sorts only by `order()` and silently chooses the first provider. DefaultCryptoProvider, WildFlyElytronProvider, and FIPS1402Provider all return 200, so when more than one is visible the winner is determined by ServiceLoader/classpath resource ordering rather than an explicit configuration. In particular, a FIPS-capable deployment that also exposes the default provider can accidentally select the non-FIPS provider instead of failing as it did previously, bypassing the intended crypto mode. Reject ties at the selected priority or define an explicit, deterministic and safe precedence.

findings.title: ES384 and ES512 tests generate P-256 keys instead of the corresponding curves
findings.body: The shared key pair is created using `KeyPairGenerator.getInstance("EC").genKeyPair()`, which uses the JVM default EC curve (normally P-256), for all three tests. Thus the ES384 and ES512 cases only exercise a P-256-sized DER signature padded to 96/132 bytes; they do not test conversion of real P-384 and P-521 signatures, including their boundary-length and leading-zero behavior. Generate keys with ECGenParameterSpec("secp384r1") and ECGenParameterSpec("secp521r1") for those algorithms.
